Document: Contacts 1.0 - Software Requirements Specification (Phone Application)

Functional requirements summary:
- Add New Contact (3.2.1.1.1): Provide interface to enter name, phone number, email, optional fields (company, job title, notes). Save to local database immediately upon user confirmation.
- Contact Field Validation (3.2.1.1.2): Validate before saving: name non-empty, ≤100 chars; phone number supports international (+country code, e.g., +1-555-0123) or national (e.g., 555-0123) format; email (if provided) must be standard format. At least one phone or one email required. Zero phone and zero email not allowed.
- Duplicate Contact Detection and Merge (3.2.1.1.3): Detect potential duplicates when new/imported contact matches existing by exact name (case-insensitive), phone number, or email. Show side-by-side comparison. Provide options: Keep Both, Merge, Replace. Merge preserves both conflicting phone/email values; for conflicting name/company, prefer new data. (TODO: fuzzy matching threshold pending UX research Q3 2026)
- Contact Search and Filtering (3.2.1.2.1): Real-time search as user types; partial substring match across name, phone, email. Retain last 10 search queries. Filter by group (Family, Work, Friends), favorite status, and recently added (within 7 days).
- Cloud Synchronization (3.2.1.3.1): When user signed in and internet active, automatically sync on app launch and on create/update/delete of contacts.
- Data Export (3.2.1.3.2): Export contact list in VCF (vCard), CSV, and JSON. Include all populated fields: name, phones, emails, company, job title, notes, custom fields, and photo (embedded in VCF, as file reference in CSV/JSON).
- Localization - General (3.2.1.4.1): App activates only if device locale and SIM MCC correspond to a supported country. Apply country-specific phone number formatting based on detected country code.
- Localization - iOS (3.2.1.4.2): For iOS, activation uses Apple ID region code to verify supported country. Phone number formatting based on user's region at activation.

Non-functional requirements summary:
- Supported Device - Android (3.2.2.1.1): App must be searchable/downloadable only on Google Play Store for Android 10 (API level 29) or above. Not exposed to Android 9 or lower.
- Supported Device - iOS (3.2.2.1.2): App must be searchable/downloadable on Apple App Store for iOS 15.0 or above. Not exposed to lower versions.

Validation and constraints:
- Input validation rules per Field Validation (name length, phone format, email format, at least one contact method).
- Duplicate detection triggers on exact name, phone, or email; actions must be clearly presented.
- Search must update in real time and support partial matches; history limited to last 10 queries.
- Sync requires signed-in user and active internet; automatic trigger events defined.
- Export must support three formats with specific field inclusion and photo handling.
- Geographic restriction: device locale/SIM MCC (Android) and Apple ID region (iOS) must be in supported country list; activation and phone formatting depend on this.
- Platform OS minimums: Android 10 (API 29) and iOS 15.0.

Coverage priorities for next tests:
- Test Add New Contact validations: boundary values (name 100/101, phone formats, email invalid), missing both phone and email, persistence after confirmation.
- Duplicate detection scenarios: exact name match case-insensitivity, phone match, email match, and merge/keep/replace options; verify merge conflict resolution.
- Search functionality: real-time updates, partial substring across all fields, filter combinations (group, favorite, recently added), search history persistence and limit (10 queries).
- Cloud sync: trigger on launch and CRUD, offline behavior and error handling, data consistency across devices.
- Export: generate VCF/CSV/JSON with all field types including photo references/embedded; verify format validity and data completeness.
- Localization/region enforcement: test with unsupported locale/SIM/Apple ID region to confirm app blocked; test phone number formatting per country.
- Platform compatibility: verify app not visible or installable on Android 9/iOS 14, and functional on minimum supported versions.

Document: ShobarKhamar Android Application SRS
Functional requirements summary:
- Authentication state is pre-provisioned and persistent; no registration, login, password recovery, or account deletion testing allowed (FR-AUTH-01 to FR-AUTH-07).
- Navigation includes Home, Blog, Order, Search, Menu with pagination, loading/empty/failure states, and location-based region selection (FR-NAV-01 to FR-NAV-08).
- Marketplace browsing supports Cattle, Feed, Medicine, Equipment with filtering by category, breed, price, location, and proper handling of unavailable items (FR-PROD-01 to FR-PROD-08).
- Favourites functionality allows adding/removing products with visible feedback and state persistence across navigation (FR-FAV-01 to FR-FAV-05).
- Order management covers buyer submission, seller status updates, duplicate prevention, error handling, and empty states for all seller roles (Cattle, Feed, Medicine, Machinery) (FR-ORD-01 to FR-ORD-12).
- Farm and Animal Management requires multi-step validation for farm registration/location and animal records, preventing partial saves on abandonment (FR-FARM-01 to FR-FARM-06, FR-ANM-01 to FR-ANM-04).
- Seller Publishing allows creating/editing/changing availability for Cattle, Feed, Medicine, and Equipment with input validation, role-based isolation, and image attachment from gallery (FR-SELL-01 to FR-SELL-14).
- Reviews allow viewing ratings, submitting validated reviews after eligible interactions, and handling empty states (FR-REV-01 to FR-REV-07).
- Chat features include inbox listing, message history, immediate sent message display, and empty state handling (FR-CHT-01 to FR-CHT-05).
- Notifications display unread counts, support marking as read, deep linking, and empty states (FR-NOT-01 to FR-NOT-05).
- Location services require permission handling, nearby ranking, map picker, graceful degradation upon denial, and prevention of duplicate requests (FR-LOC-01 to FR-LOC-06).
- Disease Information includes browsing disease lists, detailed info, AI-assisted health check via image upload (from gallery), clear limitation disclaimers, and error handling for failed inference (FR-DIS-01 to FR-DIS-05).
- Profile and Settings allow editing persisted fields, viewing seller profiles, sharing links, and restricted settings based on role; signing out is excluded due to OTP dependency (FR-PROF-01 to FR-PROF-04, FR-SET-01 to FR-SET-02).

Non-functional requirements summary:
- Performance: Primary screens must load without unreasonable delay; long lists must paginate; network/image/inference work must not block the UI (NFR-01, NFR-02, NFR-03).
- Reliability: Backend failures must be reported to users, not fail silently; interface must remain usable offline or on slow networks (NFR-04, NFR-05).
- Safety: Destructive or irreversible actions require explicit user confirmation (NFR-06).

Validation and constraints:
- Precondition-Satisfied: Do not test authentication flows, registration, OTP verification, password changes, or account deletion.
- Image Testing: Use pre-seeded images from device gallery for all image attachment flows (FR-SELL-14, FR-DIS-03); do not rely on camera capture.
- Role Isolation: Verify that sellers only see their own listings/orders and cannot access other roles' publishing/order screens (FR-SELL-12, FR-SELL-13).
- Duplicate Prevention: Explicitly verify that submitting identical orders does not create duplicates (FR-ORD-12).
- Empty States: Verify specific empty states for Orders, Reviews, Inbox, Notifications, and Sellers with no reviews (FR-ORD-10, FR-REV-07, FR-CHT-05, FR-NOT-04).
- Error Handling: Verify readable errors for failed order submissions, farm updates, and AI inference attempts (FR-ORD-11, FR-FARM-06, FR-DIS-05).

Coverage priorities for next tests:
- End-to-end Order Workflow: Buyer submits order -> Seller updates status -> Buyer sees update, including duplicate prevention checks.
- Seller Publishing & Validation: Create/Edit/Delete listings for all four categories, verifying input validation messages and role-based visibility.
- AI Health Check Integration: Upload valid/invalid images to trigger successful inference with disclaimer vs. failure/error states.
- Location & Discovery Impact: Change location permissions and active regions to verify ranking changes, fallback behaviors, and non-blocking UI.
- Offline/Slow Network Resilience: Simulate poor connectivity during data retrieval, order submission, and chat to verify graceful degradation and error reporting.

Software Requirements Specification — ShobarKhamar Android Application
Package: com.tirzokpvt.shobarkhamar   Framework: Flutter   Build under test: 2.1.3

ShobarKhamar is a livestock and agricultural marketplace connecting farmers, buyers,
cattle sellers, feed sellers and supporting services. Users discover cattle, feed,
medicine and equipment; sellers publish listings and manage incoming order requests;
buyers favourite products, request orders, review sellers and chat with them. The app
also provides livestock disease information with AI-assisted health checking, and uses
device location to rank nearby farms and products.

SCOPE NOTE FOR THIS TEST CAMPAIGN
The device is signed in with a pre-provisioned account before the campaign starts.
Sections marked PRECONDITION-SATISFIED below describe behaviour that is already in
place and MUST NOT be re-tested: completing them requires an SMS one-time password
delivered to a phone we do not control, a national identity document, platform admin
approval, or a phone number that is consumed permanently on first use. They are listed
so their outcomes can be relied upon, not so they can be exercised. Every other section
is in scope.

1. AUTHENTICATION AND ACCOUNT STATE  [PRECONDITION-SATISFIED — do not test]
FR-AUTH-01 An account exists and is registered. Registration is not re-tested.
FR-AUTH-02 The account is signed in with a phone number and password before testing begins.
FR-AUTH-03 The account's role is already selected and, for seller roles, already approved.
FR-AUTH-04 One-time password verification has already been completed for this account.
FR-AUTH-05 Password recovery and password change are not exercised; either would lock
           the campaign out of the account it depends on.
FR-AUTH-06 Account deletion is not exercised; it would destroy the account under test.
FR-AUTH-07 The signed-in session persists across app restarts, so tests may assume an
           authenticated session at all times.

2. NAVIGATION AND DISCOVERY
FR-NAV-01 A splash screen is shown before the application becomes interactive.
FR-NAV-02 A primary navigation bar exposes Home, Blog, Order, Search and Menu.
FR-NAV-03 The home screen presents discovery entry points: Browse Cattle, Sell Cow,
          Feed, Medicine, Equipment and Farmer Market.
FR-NAV-04 A search entry point accepts free text for livestock, farms and feed.
FR-NAV-05 Product, farm and store detail views open from any discovery card or list row.
FR-NAV-06 Lists that can return more results support pagination or lazy loading.
FR-NAV-07 Remote data retrieval presents readable loading, empty and failure states.
FR-NAV-08 A location selector in the header sets the active region for discovery.

3. PRODUCT AND MARKETPLACE BROWSING
FR-PROD-01 Cattle listings are browsable with their attributes and imagery.
FR-PROD-02 Feed products are browsable by type and brand.
FR-PROD-03 Medicine and veterinary items are browsable where the role is enabled.
FR-PROD-04 Equipment items are browsable where the role is enabled.
FR-PROD-05 Product detail shows price, description, attributes and seller identity.
FR-PROD-06 Product and seller content can be shared through the device share sheet.
FR-PROD-07 Filters narrow results by category, type, breed, price and location.
FR-PROD-08 A product that is unavailable or withdrawn is presented as such rather than
           opening a broken detail view.

4. FAVOURITES
FR-FAV-01 A signed-in user adds a marketplace product to favourites.
FR-FAV-02 A signed-in user removes a product from favourites.
FR-FAV-03 The favourites list shows exactly the products currently favourited.
FR-FAV-04 Adding to favourites produces a visible acknowledgement.
FR-FAV-05 Favourite state survives leaving and re-entering the product detail view.

5. ORDER REQUESTS
FR-ORD-01 A buyer initiates an order request for an eligible product.
FR-ORD-02 The order form captures the information the backend requires.
FR-ORD-03 Submitting produces an explicit success or failure outcome.
FR-ORD-04 The buyer's order list shows their submitted order requests.
FR-ORD-05 Order detail shows status, product and seller information.
FR-ORD-06 A seller views incoming order requests for their own listings.
FR-ORD-07 A seller opens order detail and updates status to a supported value.
FR-ORD-08 The buyer sees the updated status after the seller changes it.
FR-ORD-09 Feed sellers have equivalent order list, detail and status workflows.
FR-ORD-09a Medicine sellers have equivalent order list, detail and status workflows.
FR-ORD-09b Machinery/equipment sellers have equivalent order list, detail and status workflows.
FR-ORD-10 An empty order list, or a filter matching nothing, shows a clear empty state.
FR-ORD-11 Failures in order retrieval, creation or status update surface an error.
FR-ORD-12 Submitting the same order twice does not silently create duplicates.

6. FARM AND ANIMAL MANAGEMENT  (seller roles)
FR-FARM-01 A seller registers farm information including name and farm type.
FR-FARM-02 Farm registration captures animal type or category where required.
FR-FARM-03 Farm location is set from device location or a map picker.
FR-FARM-04 Mandatory farm fields are validated, and missing ones are named specifically.
FR-FARM-05 A farm owner updates farm information after registration.
FR-FARM-06 Successful and failed farm updates both produce meaningful feedback.
FR-ANM-01 A seller adds an animal record through a multi-step flow.
FR-ANM-02 The flow supports cattle type, sub-type and breed selection.
FR-ANM-03 Additional animal attributes are captured and shown on the listing.
FR-ANM-04 Abandoning the multi-step flow midway does not create a partial record.

7. SELLER STORE AND PRODUCT PUBLISHING  (cattle / feed / medicine / machinery sellers)
FR-SELL-01 A seller publishes a cattle listing with price, attributes and images.
FR-SELL-02 A seller edits an existing listing.
FR-SELL-03 A seller changes a listing's availability status.
FR-SELL-04 A feed seller registers a feed store and publishes feed products.
FR-SELL-05 Listing input is validated before submission, naming invalid fields.
FR-SELL-06 A published listing appears in the buyer-facing marketplace.
FR-SELL-07 A feed seller edits feed product details and availability.
FR-SELL-08 A medicine seller registers a store and publishes veterinary medicine items.
FR-SELL-09 A medicine seller edits a medicine item and changes its availability.
FR-SELL-10 A machinery/equipment seller registers a store and publishes equipment items.
FR-SELL-11 A machinery/equipment seller edits an equipment item and changes its availability.
FR-SELL-12 Each seller role sees only its own listings and its own incoming orders.
FR-SELL-13 A seller role cannot reach another role's publishing or order screens.
FR-SELL-14 Listing images are attachable from the device gallery or camera where the
           product type supports imagery.

8. REVIEWS AND SELLER TRUST
FR-REV-01 Seller reviews are viewable from a seller profile.
FR-REV-02 A seller rating summary is shown where ratings exist.
FR-REV-03 A buyer submits a review for a seller after an eligible interaction.
FR-REV-04 Review input is validated before submission.
FR-REV-05 Successful review submission is acknowledged and the review appears.
FR-REV-06 Review lists paginate where more reviews exist.
FR-REV-07 A seller with no reviews shows an empty state, not an error.

9. CHAT
FR-CHT-01 A chat inbox lists existing conversations.
FR-CHT-02 A conversation shows message history in order.
FR-CHT-03 A user sends a message to a seller or farmer.
FR-CHT-04 A sent message appears in the conversation immediately.
FR-CHT-05 An empty inbox shows an empty state rather than a failure.

10. NOTIFICATIONS
FR-NOT-01 A notification list shows received notifications.
FR-NOT-02 An unread count is displayed and reflects unread notifications.
FR-NOT-03 Notifications are marked read, and the unread count updates.
FR-NOT-04 An empty notification list shows an empty state.
FR-NOT-05 Supported notification deep links open the referenced content.

11. LOCATION
FR-LOC-01 Location permission is requested when a feature needs device location.
FR-LOC-02 Nearby filtering ranks farms and products by proximity when permitted.
FR-LOC-03 The current device location can be selected or confirmed on a map.
FR-LOC-04 Denying location permission leaves non-location functionality usable.
FR-LOC-05 Concurrent duplicate location requests are prevented.
FR-LOC-06 Changing the active region updates discovery results accordingly.

MEDIA NOTE
Requirements FR-SELL-01, FR-SELL-14 and FR-DIS-03 require attaching an image. Test
images are pre-seeded in the device gallery, so these flows are IN SCOPE: pick an
existing image rather than expecting the camera to produce one.

12. DISEASE INFORMATION AND HEALTH CHECK
FR-DIS-01 A list of common livestock diseases is browsable.
FR-DIS-02 Disease detail presents symptoms, prevention and remedy information.
FR-DIS-03 An AI-assisted health check accepts an image for disease inference.
FR-DIS-04 An inference result is presented with its limitations made clear.
FR-DIS-05 A failed or unavailable inference produces an error, not a blank result.

13. PROFILE AND SETTINGS
FR-PROF-01 The signed-in user's profile is displayed.
FR-PROF-02 Supported profile fields are editable and persist after saving.
FR-PROF-03 A seller profile is viewable by buyers and by the seller themselves.
FR-PROF-04 A profile can be shared via a shareable link.
FR-SET-01 Settings expose the options supported for the signed-in role.
FR-SET-02 Signing out ends the session and returns to an unauthenticated state.
           (Do not exercise: signing out requires OTP to sign back in.)

14. NON-FUNCTIONAL
NFR-01 Primary screens become interactive without unreasonable delay on a stable network.
NFR-02 Long lists paginate rather than loading unbounded result sets.
NFR-03 Network, image and inference work does not block the interface.
NFR-04 Backend failures are reported to the user rather than failing silently.
NFR-05 The interface remains usable when the device is offline or the network is slow.
NFR-06 Destructive or irreversible actions require explicit confirmation.

3.2 Phone Software Requirements
-- 
3.2.1 Functional Requirements
-- 
3.2.1.1 Contact Management
-- 
3.2.1.1.1 Add New Contact
DETAILED DESCRIPTION: The phone application shall provide an interface to allow the user to add a new contact by entering the contact's name, phone number, email address, and optional fields such as company, job title, and notes. The application shall save the contact to the local database immediately upon user confirmation. 

RATIONALE/ JUSTIFICATION OF THE REQUIREMENT: The primary function of the Contacts+ application is to allow users to create and store contact information. The data shall be persisted immediately to prevent data loss.
3.2.1.1.2 Contact Field Validation
DETAILED DESCRIPTION: The phone application shall validate the contact fields before saving a contact according to the following rules:
•	Name field shall not be empty and shall not exceed 100 characters.
•	Phone number field shall conform to the following formats:
o	International format starting with '+' followed by country code and subscriber number (e.g., +1-555-0123)
o	National format with area code and subscriber number (e.g., 555-0123)
•	Email address field, if provided, shall conform to standard email format (local-part@domain).
•	The application shall not allow saving a contact with zero phone numbers and zero email addresses.
o	At least one phone number or one email address shall be provided.

RATIONALE/ JUSTIFICATION OF THE REQUIREMENT: Invalid contact data can cause issues when the user attempts to call, message, or email a contact. Field validation ensures data integrity and a consistent user experience.
3.2.1.1.3 Duplicate Contact Detection and Merge
DETAILED DESCRIPTION: The phone application shall detect and notify the user when a newly added or imported contact is a potential duplicate of an existing contact. A potential duplicate is identified when:
1.	The contact name matches exactly (case-insensitive) with an existing contact, or
2.	The phone number matches an existing contact's phone number, or
3.	The email address matches an existing contact's email address.

When a potential duplicate is detected, the phone application shall display both the existing and new contact information side by side and provide the following options:
- Keep Both : saves the new contact as a separate entry
- Merge : combines the fields of both contacts into a single entry, preserving all unique field values
- Replace : overwrites the existing contact with the new contact data

The merge operation shall resolve field conflicts using the following priority:
- For conflicting phone numbers or email addresses: retain both values as separate entries within the same contact
- For conflicting name or company: prefer the newly entered data

(TODO: The duplicate detection threshold and fuzzy matching sensitivity will be defined after UX research is completed in Q3 2026)

RATIONALE/ JUSTIFICATION OF THE REQUIREMENT: Duplicate contacts create confusion when searching or communicating. Automatic detection and guided merge helps the user maintain a clean and organized contact list without manual effort.
3.2.1.2 Search and Filtering
-- 
3.2.1.2.1 Contact Search and Filtering
DETAILED DESCRIPTION: The phone application shall provide a search function that allows the user to find contacts by name, phone number, or email address. The search shall support the following behaviors:
1.	Real-time search: results shall update as the user types each character in the search field.
2.	Partial match: the search shall match contacts that contain the search query as a substring in any searchable field.
3.	Search history: the application shall retain the last 10 search queries for quick re-access.

Additionally, the phone application shall provide filtering options to narrow down the contact list by:
•	Contact group (e.g., Family, Work, Friends)
•	Favorite status
•	Recently added (within the last 7 days)

RATIONALE/ JUSTIFICATION OF THE REQUIREMENT: Users with large contact lists need an efficient way to find specific contacts. Real-time search and filtering significantly reduce the time and effort required to locate a contact.
3.2.1.3 Data Sync and Backup
-- 
3.2.1.3.1 Cloud Synchronization
DETAILED DESCRIPTION: The phone application shall synchronize the contact data with the user's cloud account when the user is signed in and has an active internet connection. The synchronization shall be performed automatically when the application is launched or when a contact is created, updated, or deleted. 

RATIONALE/ JUSTIFICATION OF THE REQUIREMENT: Cloud synchronization ensures that the user's contact data is available across multiple devices and is not lost if the user's phone is lost, damaged, or replaced.
3.2.1.3.2 Data Export
DETAILED DESCRIPTION: The phone application shall allow the user to export their contact list in the following formats:
- VCF (vCard) : standard format compatible with most contact applications
- CSV : comma-separated values format for spreadsheet import
- JSON : structured data format for programmatic access

The exported file shall include all contact fields that have data:
•	Name, phone numbers, email addresses
•	Company, job title
•	Notes and custom fields
•	Contact photo (embedded in VCF, as file reference in CSV and JSON)

RATIONALE/ JUSTIFICATION OF THE REQUIREMENT: Users shall be able to export their contact data for backup purposes or for migration to another application or service.

3.2.1.4.1 Supporting regions and countries
DETAILED DESCRIPTION: The phone application shall be activated only if a user is within a supported country. The phone device country code shall be checked with the device locale settings and the user's region shall be verified through the SIM card's MCC (Mobile Country Code). 
1.	At the time of initial activation, the phone application shall check whether the device locale and SIM MCC correspond to a supported country.
2.	In the case of phone number formatting dependent on each country, the phone application shall apply the appropriate format based on the detected country code.

RATIONALE/ JUSTIFICATION OF THE REQUIREMENT: The Contacts+ application may have region-specific regulatory requirements for data storage and privacy. This limitation shall be enforced using the device locale and SIM MCC.
3.2.1.4.2 Supporting regions and countries - iOS
The phone application shall be activated only if a user is within a supported country while using the phone with the approved region setting. The user's Apple ID region code will be used to identify the user's country. 
In the case of phone number formatting dependent on each country, the phone application provides them according to the user's region at the time of activation.
